mode_evidence: Breath nimitta and light of concentration are described as seen (light before the nimitta, cotton wool, morning star, 'wherever you look, you see only white'); but Pa-Auk also says the nimitta is 'produced by perception', can be made long, short or red at will, and tells the yogi to 'visualize' kasinas with eyes closed until the nimitta is seen 'as clearly as if you were looking at it with your eyes open', which is imaginal crossing. He does not say that the white is in the retinal visual field.
onset_evidence: Induction: hold the breath at its touch point and ignore any nimitta far away; the nimitta comes and stays there. For kasinas, look at the object with eyes open, then close and visualize; if unable, re-establish the fourth anapana jhana and look with the light of concentration, or use a skeleton white until only a white circle remains. Time scales: hold the white sign one, two, three hours or more; the skeleton fades after one or two hours of white. The digest shows no statement that light cannot be forced, other than do not play with the nimitta; a nimitta far in front is not a real one.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Earth kasina: eyes open a while, then closed. Fire kasina: screen with circular hole before a wood or grass fire. Light kasina: rays through a wall crack or leaves, or a lamp in an earthen pot with light falling on a wall.
conditions.duration_and_schedule: One, two, three hours or more fixed on the white sign.
conditions.prerequisites: Fourth anapana jhana gives the light needed for skeleton and white kasina.

stages.label: parikamma-nimitta
stages.description: Natural breath and touch point; smoky grey may appear around the nostrils.

stages.label: uggaha-nimitta
stages.description: Grey becomes white like cotton wool, usually dull and opaque.

stages.label: patibhaga-nimitta
stages.description: Bright, clear, radiant like the morning star; access or absorption concentration.

stages.label: expanded white kasina
stages.description: White circle expanded by a set number of inches in stages until it fills all ten directions.

what_to_do_with_light: Do not play with the nimitta, change its shape, or shift to it early; keep the mind on the touch point until the nimitta is stable and merged with the breath, then rest on it for hours until it brightens; then, in kasina practice, expand it in determined stages and use the light of concentration to discern body parts.
obstacles_and_fixes: Nimitta appears far in front: ignore it; concentrate at the touch point.
Colour and shape changing often: ignore them and attend to it as the breath nimitta.
Expanded white unstable: return to noting 'white - white'.
Unable to visualize the kasina: re-establish the fourth anapana jhana and use its light.
cautions: Playing with the nimitta halts progress and it will probably disappear.
A nimitta far from the nostrils is not a real breath nimitta.
Forcing the mind off a stable nimitta may lose concentration.
interpretation: The nimitta is mind-born, produced by perception and the level of concentration; the light of concentration is the light of wisdom that lets the yogi see ultimate mentality-materiality.
practice_summary: Keep attention on the touch point of the breath. For some yogis a light appears first, for others a nimitta directly: grey smoke, then white like cotton wool. If it appears far out in front, ignore it; stay at the touch point and it will come there. When it is stable, merged with the breath, drop the breath and attend to it alone. Do not change or play with it. Keep your mind on the white sign for one, two or three hours until it becomes bright as the morning star. Then, for the white kasina, use that light to discern a skeleton, fix on its whitest spot as 'white - white' until only a white circle remains, and expand it in set stages until white fills all directions.

key_passages.anchor: For some yogis, there is first light before the nimitta appears, for others, the nimitta appears directly.
key_passages.paraphrase: A light may precede the nimitta, and the two are distinct, as the sun differs from sunlight.

key_passages.anchor: If you ignore it, and simply concentrate on the breath at the place where the breath touches, the nimitta will come and stay there.
key_passages.paraphrase: For someone with no stable nimitta, keep at the touch point and ignore distant lights.

key_passages.anchor: it is important not to play with your nimitta. Do not let it go away, and do not intentionally change its shape
key_passages.paraphrase: Altering or toying with the nimitta ends progress.

key_passages.anchor: When you are able to concentrate on the white for one or two hours, you will find that the skeleton disappears and only a white circle remains.
key_passages.paraphrase: Sustained fixing on white makes the skeleton fade leaving a white circle, the uggaha-nimitta.
key_passages.quote: When you are able to concentrate on the white for one or two hours, you will find that the skeleton disappears and only a white circle remains.

key_passages.anchor: Concentrate on it for a while with your eyes open, and then close them, and visualize the earth kasina.
key_passages.paraphrase: Kasina sign is first taken with eyes open, then visualized with eyes closed, with a fallback of using the light of concentration.

confidence_note: Digest only; the four stages of breath practice and the Q&A on the light of concentration were not seen.
